_meta.description: Locked 12-question eval dataset for the Personal Portfolio Copilot capstone. See Personal Portfolio Copilot-prd.md Task 1 §4 for the source table and methodology note. Thesis concept retired -- questions previously comparing content against a user's free-text thesis now test either objective driver-identification (Q1) or the Fundamentals Health Score (Q2, Q7, Q11, Q13).

scoring_methods.ragas_triad: RAGAS Faithfulness, LLMContextRecall, FactualCorrectness against a written reference answer. Session 6 / harness shape per Session 10 run_eval.py.
scoring_methods.tool_call_goal_topic: Tool-call accuracy (right tool, right args), goal accuracy (final answer satisfies the request), topic adherence (stays grounded in the user's actual holdings and Fundamentals Health Score, not thesis). Normalized from a LangGraph trace, per Session 6.
scoring_methods.deterministic_assertion: Exact-match / tolerance-based assertion against a computed ground-truth value (e.g. gain/loss math) -- not an LLM judge.
scoring_methods.hybrid: Deterministic assertion for a numeric sub-component, plus tool_call_goal_topic for the reasoning/synthesis wrapped around it.

questions.question_template: What did {company}'s management identify as the specific driver behind {metric}?
questions.expected_behavior: Retrieves the exact quoted driver management cited (not a generic mention), distinguishes backward-looking results from forward-looking guidance, cites the exact transcript section.
questions.reuses: test_q1.py's load_ticker_documents/build_retriever (generic utilities, unchanged) + a new driver-identification prompt defined in run_eval.py -- test_q1.py's original Verdict/Evidence/Explanation thesis-comparison prompt is retired along with the thesis concept and is no longer used by this question.

test_cases.reference: Non-GAAP gross margin was 76.4%, up 70 basis points from the previous quarter, attributed to a lower mix of hardware sales within signal conditioning.
Fiscal Q2 2026 non-GAAP gross margin guidance of approximately 73%, including a 200 basis point non-cash impact from a one-time customer agreement.

Company (overall) gross margin was 49.3%, up 110 basis points sequentially, driven by favorable mix and lower tariff-related costs, partly offset by seasonal loss of leverage and higher memory costs; product gross margin alone decreased 200 basis points sequentially on seasonal loss of leverage and higher memory costs.
June quarter (fiscal Q3 2026) gross margin guidance of 47.5%-48.5%, driven primarily by significantly higher expected memory costs, partially offset by the benefit of carry-in inventory.

test_cases.metric: this quarter's data center revenue growth
test_cases.reference: Data center revenue was $1.8 billion (76% of total revenue), up 11% sequentially and 27% year-over-year, with growth achieved across optical interconnect, custom silicon, and switching products.

test_cases.metric: fiscal 2028 data center revenue growth guidance
test_cases.reference: Fiscal 2028 data center revenue guidance of approximately 55% year-over-year growth, accelerating from fiscal 2027, driven by interconnect growth (1.6T scale-out demand plus scale-up/scale-across contributions), custom silicon revenue more than doubling, and continued Ethernet switching ramp.

test_cases.metric: this quarter's adjusted EBITDA margin change
test_cases.reference: Nebius AI business adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 45% in Q1 2026, up from 24% in Q4 2025, an improvement management attributed to strong revenue growth (Nebius AI revenue up 841% year-over-year, 82% quarter-over-quarter) driving operating leverage.

Management guided fiscal Q2 2026 group adjusted EBITDA margin to step down sequentially from Q1 levels before returning to Q1 levels in Q3 and moving higher in Q4, driven by the timing of upfront investments (hiring, recent acquisitions, product development) landing before the back-end-weighted capacity and revenue they support comes online -- a timing dynamic, not a structural change, per CFO Dado Alonso.

Total gross margin for the quarter was 75.8%, including services gross margin of 75.1%; product gross margin was 78.8%, a 40 basis point improvement year over year, balanced by driving cloud-hosting efficiencies against the mix shift toward higher-growth SaaS offerings.

test_cases.metric: fiscal Q4 2026 revenue and margin outlook
test_cases.reference: Fiscal Q4 2026 guidance of $3.345 billion to $3.355 billion in revenue (about 32% growth); full fiscal-year 2026 operating margin guided to 28.9%-29.2%. Management cited acceleration in Q3 organic bookings growth, early M&A integration progress, and a strong Q4 pipeline as the basis for raising full-year guidance across NGS ARR, RPO, and revenue.

Gross margin dollars increased 18% year over year to $6.8 billion; gross margin rate was 20.5%, slightly better than anticipated, reflecting a mix shift toward AI servers (AI revenue up more than 4x year over year) and improved profitability in storage.

Management guided FY2027 gross margin rate up year-over-year excluding AI mix impact, citing pricing actions to protect margin rates (already visible in the ISG segment, with CSG improvements beginning in Q1 and continuing through the year) amid a tight supply environment and rising input costs.

questions.question_template: What's the latest news on {company}, and does it affect my position?
questions.expected_behavior: Live search (Tavily) for recent news, cross-referenced against the ticker's current Fundamentals Health Score; flags relevance high/medium/low with source links, noting whether the news touches any Monitor/At-Risk signal.
questions.reuses: test_q2.py (search_tavily, topic=general, RELEVANCE_PROMPT) -- RELEVANCE_PROMPT needs updating to compare against Fundamentals Health Score status instead of a stored thesis string

questions.question_template: Has {company}'s tone or substance changed on {risk_or_opportunity} across its last 4 earnings calls?
questions.expected_behavior: Synthesizes across 4 chronologically-ordered transcripts, identifies whether language or emphasis on the named topic shifted (introduced, dropped, escalated, softened), cites which call each shift occurred in. Tests longitudinal narrative-drift detection -- catching gradual changes a user would otherwise miss by only skimming 1-2 headlines a week (Problem Statement, Section 3).
questions.reuses: test_q1.py's load/retriever logic + a new chronological-synthesis prompt -- NOT built. Still blocked on data, not just the prompt: only 1 quarter of transcript is currently ingested per ticker (e.g. ALAB has only transcript_Q1_2026.txt); needs 3 more historical quarters fetched before this is runnable at all.

test_cases.risk_or_opportunity: TBD -- pick a real recurring topic once 4 quarters of transcripts are ingested

questions.question_template: Is there any insider selling in my holdings this week?
questions.expected_behavior: Queries insider-transaction data, filters to the user's portfolio tickers only, returns relevant Form 4 activity.

questions.question_template: Has there been any recent {topic} mentioned in {company}'s filings?
questions.expected_behavior: Agent must recognize the question demands complete/exhaustive recall -- missing a real disclosure is a genuine failure, not a minor gap -- and route to keyword/exact-match search rather than lossy top-k vector retrieval (a previously-demonstrated failure mode: k=6 missed a real match). Returns a synthesized, cited answer that distinguishes routine boilerplate risk-factor language from an active, material signal, rather than just dumping raw matches.
questions.reuses: test_q7.py (build_pattern regex, find_hits with ±200 char context, dedupe_hits, format_single_hit) + SUMMARY_PROMPT synthesis pass, so the response is structurally comparable to the reference instead of a raw snippet dump

test_cases.question: Has there been any recent capacity or demand problems mentioned in Astera Labs's filings?
test_cases.reference: Yes, both terms appear, but the substance skews toward strength, not weakness: 15 'capacity' mentions (14 in the 10-K, mostly standard manufacturing-dependency risk factors; 1 in the transcript, an analyst Q&A on inventory/capacity) and 72 'demand' mentions (62 in the 10-K, largely boilerplate risk language; 5 in the 10-Q including the MD&A line attributing Q1 2026's $308.4M revenue to 'a sizable increase in demand'; 5 in the transcript citing strong customer demand). No disclosure describes an active capacity shortfall or demand shortfall as a current event.

test_cases.question: Has Astera Labs disclosed any customer concentration risk recently?
test_cases.reference: Yes, but only as generic risk-factor boilerplate -- the identical sentence appears once in the 10-K and once in the 10-Q ('our customer concentration, with a limited number of end customers driving our revenue'), with no specific customer, percentage, or magnitude named. Not a disclosure of a new or worsening concentration event.

questions.question_template: What did analysts say after today's {event}?
questions.expected_behavior: Live search synthesis with dated, sourced citations distinguishing analyst commentary from company statements.
questions.reuses: test_q8.py (3-bucket ANALYST_PROMPT, fetch_recommendation_trends as authoritative institutional data)

questions.question_template: {company} just dropped {move_pct}% today, I'm nervous -- should I sell?
questions.expected_behavior: Does not validate the fear reflexively; checks the drop against the ticker's actual Fundamentals Health Score signals (revenue/margin/insider/leadership) and recent filings/news, and states plainly whether anything changed -- separates signal from noise instead of mirroring the user's emotional framing. Parametrized across ticker/move size, not hardcoded to one scenario.
questions.reuses: test_q7_grounding.py: calls the real deployed agent (app.graph.ask) against all 3 locked test cases, checks it called a live data-checking tool, and has an independent LLM judge score topic_adherence/goal_accuracy/tool_call_accuracy. Verified: 3 of 3 cases PASS on all three criteria -- the agent grounds every response in a specific signal (health score status, insider activity, analyst ratings, or live price) rather than validating or dismissing the user's fear reflexively. NBIS case notably caught that the described 12% drop didn't match the actual live price (+1.6%) and said so.

questions.question_template: Have analysts changed their rating on {company} recently?
questions.expected_behavior: Queries Finnhub recommendation-trends, compares the current period to prior period(s), states whether the buy/hold/sell distribution shifted and by how much, with period dates cited.
questions.reuses: test_q8.py --mode rating_change: fetch_recommendation_trends + compute_trend_deltas (deterministic Python diff between the two most recent periods) + RATING_CHANGE_PROMPT (LLM narrates the precomputed deltas, does not recompute them). Verified via two real runs against MRVL: correctly reported a 1-analyst buy-rating increase (29->30) with all other categories unchanged, both period dates cited.

questions.question_template: Summarize everything notable about {company} this week -- filings, media, and analyst activity.
questions.expected_behavior: Synthesizes across all three signal categories (filings/keyword checks, Tavily media search, Finnhub institutional consensus) into one digest, each item cited to source and date.
questions.reuses: test_q9.py: calls the real deployed agent with the eval's own question wording, checks tool-call coverage across all 3 named categories (filings/media/analyst), independent LLM judge scores source_coverage/citation_quality/tool_call_accuracy. Real run against ALAB first surfaced a defect: agent called search_live_news + get_market_data but never a filings tool, yet its summary asserted 'No new filings or 8-K disclosures were found this week' as a checked fact -- an ungrounded claim, not just a skipped tool. A prompt-only fix (STABLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT rule) improved Q7 as a side effect but did not fix Q9 (2 re-runs, same miss). Fixed with a deterministic code-level guard in app/graph.py's ask(): if the question names filings and the trace skipped a filings tool, call search_filings directly and force a correction turn instructing the model to add/correct only the filings section while preserving the rest verbatim. First correction-turn version regressed citation detail on market/news sections (new FAILs on citation_quality/tool_call_accuracy, different reason than the original bug); tightened the correction prompt to explicitly require preserving prior detail. Re-run against ALAB: all 3 criteria PASS (source_coverage, citation_quality, tool_call_accuracy), with real filing citations (10-Q 2026-05-06, 8-K 2026-06-08) alongside full market/news/analyst detail. Q7 re-verified unaffected (still 3/3 PASS).

questions.question_template: When does {company} report next, and what should I watch for based on its current Fundamentals Health Score?
questions.expected_behavior: Surfaces the next earnings date and names the specific sub-signal(s) -- revenue growth, margin, insider activity, leadership stability -- that the upcoming report will test, especially any currently at Monitor or At Risk.
questions.reuses: test_q11.py: precomputes real ground truth (fetch_next_earnings_date + get_fundamentals_health_score, both already used by the live agent) before asking the agent anything, then deterministically checks the response cites the exact earnings date and names every flagged sub-signal, plus an LLM judge for goal_accuracy/topic_adherence/no_overclaiming. Two test cases: MRVL (has a real monitor/at_risk signal to catch) and NBIS (insufficient_data on revenue/margin -- tests honest reporting of that gap, not invention).

questions.question_template: What happened across my whole portfolio this week that I should know about?
questions.expected_behavior: Synthesizes across all held tickers, only surfaces items that would clear the alert-relevance threshold, cites each with source and date -- a pull-based version of what a proactive digest would push.
questions.reuses: extends Q9's orchestration across all 4 tickers, adds the relevance-threshold filter -- not built

questions.question_template: Has anything about {company}'s underlying business gotten worse since I bought it -- revenue, margins, insider activity, or leadership?
questions.expected_behavior: Runs the four-signal Fundamentals Health Score (Task 2 §4): reports each sub-signal's status and the overall worst-of rollup, with the specific numbers/events driving any non-intact rating. Deliberately scored as a CURRENT-STATE answer, not a true point-in-time diff against date_purchased -- no historical health-score snapshot exists anywhere in this codebase, so a correct response reports current status honestly rather than fabricating a since-you-bought-it comparison it has no data to support (see PRD Open Items).
questions.reuses: test_q13.py: precomputes real ground truth (get_fundamentals_health_score, already computed for every live agent turn) before asking the agent anything, then deterministically checks all four sub-signal names are addressed and the worst-of overall status is reflected, plus an LLM judge for rollup_accuracy/signal_completeness/honest_framing. Six-attempt fix history, full detail in the PRD's Open Items: (1) prompt-only rule in STABLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT -- insufficient; (2) response-side keyword ban-list -- evaded by paraphrase ('have not gotten worse... remain intact or improved'); (3) same classifier gated by a question-side keyword list -- same brittleness one level removed; (4) ungated LLM classifier plus an appended disclaimer -- the classifier correctly detected the overclaim, but the disclaimer sat after a comparison claim already made earlier in the same response, so the message still contradicted itself; (5) the model removed from the framing decision entirely -- get_fundamentals_health_score()'s already-deterministic signal statuses rendered directly as a fixed Python-formatted block (_render_current_status_block in app/graph.py) and prepended to every answer, model instructed to add only supporting detail underneath it. A real run against ALAB after (5) caught a further gap: rollup_accuracy and honest_framing PASSed but signal_completeness FAILed -- margin was never mentioned, because margin and revenue_growth are computed directly from XBRL data inside get_fundamentals_health_score() and never go through an agent tool call, so the narrative composer (which only reads tool-call outputs) had nothing to say about them; (6) _render_signal_facts() added to hand the composer every signal's raw supporting numbers regardless of source (tool call or direct XBRL fetch). Re-run against ALAB: all three criteria PASS (rollup_accuracy, signal_completeness, honest_framing). Real RAGAS ToolCallAccuracy also scored 1.00 on the same run.
